author: j-fischer
body:
## Summary
• **Introduced Field Visibility Settings**: Added field visibility button and panel with compact dropdown menu using native Lightning components to remove individual portions from log messages in the log message viewer
• **Display of JSON content**: Improved log event viewer to display JSON embedded into log message in a dedicated UI, making it easier to read
• **Improved Empty State**: Introduced a message for when no log event is selected to improve user guidance
• **Message Highlighting**: Added row colors for log messages by log level for easier identification of different log event types
• **Full-screen Log Even Viewer**: Added button to put log event viewer into full screen mode to increase readability of the log messages

author: reisene
body:
## Podsumowanie zmian (Sourcery)

Dodano obsługę SEO i PWA, zgodną z GDPR Politykę Prywatności i strony RODO z dynamicznym spisem treści, ikony mediów społecznościowych/wsparcia w nagłówku oraz rezerwowy JS dla starszych przeglądarek; refaktoryzacja stylów do modułów SCSS i podział JavaScript na moduły ES; wprowadzono potok CI dla automatycznego testowania i wdrażania.

Nowe funkcje:
- Dodano kompleksową Politykę Prywatności i strony RODO ze zgodną z GDPR zawartością i pływającym spisem treści
- Osadzono ikony mediów społecznościowych i wsparcia w nagłówku strony
- Wdrożono bogate SEO: metadane (opis, słowa kluczowe, Open Graph, karty Twittera), favikony, linki kanoniczne i manifest webowy dla obsługi PWA
- Wprowadzono dynamiczny przełącznik spisu treści dla stron z polityką i manifest PWA dla obsługi offline/instalacji
- Zapewniono rezerwowy JS dla starszych przeglądarek (przyklejony nagłówek, płynne przewijanie, aktualizacje stopki)

Ulepszenia:
- Przebudowano CSS na udokumentowane części SCSS (mixiny, zmienne, struktura modułowa)
- Zrefaktoryzowano JavaScript na moduły ES (footer, toc, stickywrapper) z ulepszoną obsługą błędów i logiką inicjalizacji

author: sidneycogdill
body:
Deprecates PR https://github.com/microsoft/proxy/pull/301. Resolves issue #300.

This does the following changes:

- Rename CMake project and target names, as well as their generated config file names.
- Add the CMake target alias with namespace prefix. This has the advantage that if the target name is missing, CMake will early fail at configure time instead of at build time.
- Modify the Proxy 4 implementation to reference `pro::v4::` instead of `pro::`.
- Rename C++ module name.
- Rename macro names.
- Add shim headers.

Note: This does **NOT** make it possible for Proxy 3 and Proxy 4 to work within the same project. The reason is due to the use of `inline namespace v4` in Proxy 4 while Proxy 3 declares everything under `pro::` namespace. When both versions are included, the error `reference to 'XXX' is ambiguous` will be emitted.

I've locally tested to confirm that removing the `inline` from `inline namespace` makes it possible for both Proxy 3 and Proxy 4 to compile within the same TU (which also confirms that all implementations now correctly reference the `pro::v4` namsepace, unlike https://github.com/microsoft/proxy/pull/301 which won't compile when `inline` is removed from `inline namespace`).

This will also make sure that a future Proxy 5 will work with Proxy 4 together, as long as the user explicitly requests the `pro::v4::` / `pro::v5::` namespace.

This PR does not include the necessary tests to verify running Proxy 3 (`3.3.0` tag) and Proxy 4 at the same time. However, that can be added in a separate PR if it's desired. Doing so will require introducing a new feature gate macro that controls the use of `inline` of `inline namespace`.

Please, look at the individual commits, instead of the 20 changed files as a whole. I've made sure that each commit correctly tracks the incremental changes. It happens that GitHub doesn't correctly track the changes and thinks that I wrote the entire `proxy/v4/proxy.h` myself.

author: xingliu0923
body:
---

## Support for OpenAI-Compatible Embedder Models (e.g., Qwen)

This PR introduces support for embedding models that adhere to the **OpenAI API compatibility standard**. This allows deepwiki-open to leverage a wider range of self-hosted or commercially available models beyond just OpenAI's official offerings for embedding tasks.

---

### Key Changes

* **Flexible Embedder Configuration:** The embedder now supports a new `type` that allows for specifying OpenAI-compatible API endpoints.
* **Example Configuration Provided:** A sample configuration file, `api/config/embedder_openai_compatible.json.bak`, is included to demonstrate how to set up an OpenAI-compatible embedder, using Qwen as an example.

---

### Benefits

* **Increased Model Versatility:** Users can now utilize various open-source or private models that offer an OpenAI-compatible API for embeddings.
* **Enhanced Customization:** Provides greater control over the embedding process by allowing the use of models tailored to specific needs or datasets.
* **Potential Cost Savings:** Enables the use of self-hosted models, which can be more cost-effective for high-volume embedding tasks.

---

### How to Use

To utilize an OpenAI-compatible embedder, you'll need to:

1.  **Set Environment Variables:**
    * `OPENAI_API_BASE_URL`: Set this environment variable to the base URL of your OpenAI-compatible API endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8000/v1`).
    * `OPENAI_API_KEY`: If your API requires an API key, set this environment variable accordingly. Keep in mind that some self-hosted solutions might not require this.

2.  **Configure `embedder.json`:**
    * Refer to the provided example configuration file: `api/config/embedder_openai_compatible.json.bak`.
    * In your `embedder.json` file, you'll need to specify the **`initialize_kwargs`** variable. This variable allows you to pass additional initialization arguments to the embedder, such as the specific model name you wish to use (e.g., `{"model": "Qwen/Qwen-7B-Chat"}`).

---

### Local Testing Confirmation

**Local testing has been successfully completed and confirmed to be working as expected.**

---

This enhancement significantly broadens the capabilities of deepwiki-open. Let me know if you have any questions or feedback!

author: bob-friedman
body:
This commit introduces a Python script (`process_usher_branch_mutations.py`) to aid in processing the output of `matUtils dump -m` for more detailed analysis of branch-specific mutations from UShER MAT files.

Key changes:
- Created a new directory `docs/virus_biology_and_analysis/scripts/`.
- Added the new Python script `process_usher_branch_mutations.py` to this directory. The script uses `dendropy` and `pandas` to parse a Newick tree and a `matUtils dump -m` output file, then associates mutations with tree nodes.
- Updated Section 7 of `docs/virus_biology_and_analysis/usher_toolkit_report.md`:
    - Removed the embedded conceptual Python code block.
    - Added a reference and relative link to the new standalone `process_usher_branch_mutations.py` script.

author: copilot
body:
Adds a new interactive morse code platformer game plugin that teaches users morse code through engaging 2D gameplay.

## Overview

This plugin implements a creative approach to learning morse code by combining it with a platformer-style game. Players control a character that moves through procedurally generated levels by entering correct morse code sequences.

## Key Features

- **Interactive 2D Platformer**: Visual game world with platforms, player character, and goal
- **Morse Code Learning**: Players must enter correct morse code (dots and dashes) to move forward
- **Procedural Generation**: Each level is randomly generated for daily practice variety
- **Progressive Difficulty**: 3 levels with increasing complexity and platform layouts
- **Lives System**: Forgiving gameplay with 3 chances before moving backward
- **Multiple Input Methods**: 
  - Click buttons for dot/dash input
  - Keyboard support (`.` for dot, `-` for dash)
- **Visual Feedback**: Clear indicators for correct/incorrect input with morse code hints
- **Complete Morse Code Support**: Full alphabet and numbers (A-Z, 0-9)

## Gameplay Mechanics

1. Player sees their character on a platform and a target letter to input
2. They enter the corresponding morse code using dots and dashes
3. Correct input moves the character forward; incorrect input costs a life
4. After 3 wrong attempts, the character moves backward
5. Goal is to reach the end flag to complete the level
6. 3 levels total with procedurally generated layouts

## Technical Implementation

- Built using the existing HabitBridge plugin architecture
- Reuses morse code mapping from the existing morse-code plugin
- Canvas-free implementation using HTML/CSS for broad compatibility
- Responsive design with consistent HabitBridge styling
- Proper game state management and progression logic

The plugin follows the established patterns from other HabitBridge plugins while introducing a unique gamified learning experience for morse code practice.

Fixes #8.

---

author: dalevyy
body:
# Overview
This PR adds support for lists into C Minor, closing #12.

# Description
Lists act as dynamic arrays in C Minor. A user is able to dynamically adjust the list during the runtime execution of a C Minor program. This is facilitated with the addition of list command statements such as `append`, `insert`, and `remove` which are now available to C Minor users.

This PR also changes how inheritance works behind the scenes to better facilitate the use of `Retype` statements.

body:
🎯 Drag & Drop Import System v5.0/6.0
📋 Übersicht
Vollständige Überarbeitung des Import-Systems mit einem modularen Drag & Drop Framework, das alle Dokumenttypen (Gewerbeakten, Personenprüfungsakten, Anträge) unterstützt.
🚀 Neue Features
Drag & Drop Core System

Universelle Drag & Drop Zonen: Import-Bereiche und Textareas unterstützen jetzt Drag & Drop für Dateien und Text
Automatische Seitenerkennung: System erkennt automatisch den Dokumenttyp (Gewerbeakte/Personenprüfung/Antrag)
Konfirmationsdialoge: Benutzer werden vor Auto-Import gefragt und können den Vorgang bestätigen/abbrechen
Toast-Benachrichtigungen: Elegante Erfolgs- und Fehlermeldungen in der oberen rechten Ecke

Spezialisierte Handler

DragDropGewerbeakte v5.0: Vollständiges Mitarbeiter-Handling mit Inhaber & Stellvertretern
DragDropAntrag v5.0: Unterstützt alle Antragstypen (Gewerbeantrag, Gewerbeauslage, Gewerbekutsche, Gewerbetelegramm)
SimpleDragDropPersonenpruefung v6.0: Ultra-einfacher Ansatz mit robuster Ergebnis-Erkennung

🔧 Import System Verbesserungen
Robuste Text-Parsing

Mehrfache Parsing-Strategien: Fallback-Methoden wenn Standard-Regex versagt
Flexible Field-Extraktion: Unterstützt verschiedene Discord-Formate und Code-Block-Varianten
Bessere Validierung: Strenge Dokumenttyp-Erkennung verhindert falsche Imports

Smart Form Filling

Automatisches Datum-Setting: Importierte Daten erhalten automatisch das aktuelle Datum (Jahr 1899)
Mitarbeiter-Management: Intelligente Zuordnung von Inhaber und Stellvertretern
Radio-Button Handling: Präzise Erkennung von Prüfungsergebnissen (Bestanden/Nicht bestanden/Ausstehend)

UX Optimierungen

Import-Button Status: Dynamische Aktivierung basierend auf Textinhalt
Auto-Collapse: Import-Bereiche klappen nach erfolgreichem Import automatisch zu
Visuelles Feedback: Drag-Over-Styling und Hover-Effekte
Verbesserte Fehlerbehandlung: Spezifische Fehlermeldungen für jeden Dokumenttyp

🎨 UI/UX Enhancements

Drag & Drop Hints: Benutzerfreundliche Hinweise "oder Akte hierher ziehen"
Responsive Styling: Funktioniert auf Desktop und mobilen Geräten
Consistent Design: Einheitliches Design-System mit Western-Theme-Farben
Progressive Enhancement: Funktioniert auch ohne Drag & Drop (Fallback zu Copy/Paste)

🔄 Migration & Compatibility

Backward Compatible: Bestehende Copy/Paste Funktionalität bleibt erhalten
Global Function Override: Nahtlose Integration in bestehende Codebase
Modular Architecture: Einfache Erweiterung für neue Dokumenttypen

Das neue System macht das Importieren von Discord-Akten deutlich benutzerfreundlicher und robuster, während es gleichzeitig die Fehlerrate durch bessere Validierung und Parsing reduziert.

author: zacxxx
body:
Previously, ActivityCards other than 'camp' (such as 'Quest Log', 'NPCs & Quests', 'Trading Hub', 'Research', 'Crafting') had their GIF backgrounds rendered almost invisibly on hover. This was due to the shared background container having a very low opacity (`opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-20`) intended for subtle SVG display, which also affected the GIF.

This commit modifies `ActivityCard.tsx` to adjust the opacity of the background image container. The logic now ensures that if a card is hovered and its `gifBackgroundImage` is active, the container's opacity is increased to `opacity-70` (matching the 'camp' card's behavior). This makes the GIFs for all relevant cards clearly visible on hover as intended. Static SVG backgrounds on non-camp cards will retain their subtle hover effect when no GIF is active.

body:
### **User description** This commit includes all necessary configurations and documentation to enable deployment of the SoulSeer monorepo (React frontend and FastAPI backend) to Vercel. Key changes and preparations: 1. **Vercel Configuration (`vercel.json`):** * Created a root `vercel.json` file to manage monorepo deployment. * Defines build processes for the frontend (React) and backend (FastAPI). * Implements routing rules: * API requests (`/api/*`) are directed to the backend. * Static assets are served with appropriate caching headers. * SPA fallback ensures client-side routing for the React app. * Removed `frontend/vercel.json` as it's superseded by the root configuration. 2. **Build Scripts & Dependencies:** * Verified `frontend/package.json` uses the standard `react-scripts build`. * Cleaned and verified `backend/requirements.txt` to include only necessary runtime dependencies. 3. **Environment Variable Handling:** * Identified all required environment variables for both frontend (e.g., `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL`, `REACT_APP_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`) and backend (e.g., `DATABASE_URL`, `JWT_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`). * Created/Updated `frontend/.env.example` and `backend/.env.example` to list these variables with placeholders. 4. **Database Connectivity:** * Confirmed the backend's database connection logic in `backend/server.py` correctly uses the `DATABASE_URL` environment variable. 5. **CORS Configuration (Backend):** * Updated `backend/server.py` to dynamically configure CORS `allow_origins` based on the `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` environment variable. This allows flexible and secure configuration for different deployment environments. 6. **Deployment Documentation:** * Generated a comprehensive markdown deployment guide (`vercel_deployment_guide.md`) detailing step-by-step instructions for you to deploy the application on Vercel. This includes project setup, environment variable configuration, and post-deployment checks. * Prepared instructions for local testing using `vercel dev`. No specific issues were encountered during this preparation phase. The application should now be ready for you to attempt deployment on Vercel following the provided guidelines. ___ ### **PR Type** Enhancement, Documentation ___ ### **Description** - Added root-level Vercel configuration for monorepo deployment. - Defines builds for backend (FastAPI) and frontend (React). - Implements custom routing and caching rules. - Enhanced backend CORS configuration to use environment variable. - Reads allowed origins from `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` with sensible defaults. - Cleaned and updated backend dependencies for production deployment. - Removed dev/test packages, clarified runtime requirements. - Added example environment variable files for backend deployment. - Documents all required backend environment variables. - Provided backend Vercel config example for reference. ___ ### **Changes walkthrough** 📝

author: hossain-khan
body:
This commit enhances the reliability of the WatchdogService by addressing key areas in app monitoring and service behavior:

1.  **Corrected Recent App Checking:**
    - I modified `RecentAppChecker.getRecentlyRunningAppStats` to accurately use the provided time interval (derived from your configured check interval in `WatchdogService`) when querying `UsageStatsManager`. Previously, it used a fixed window and a limited subset of results.
    - I ensured that all apps active within the specified interval are considered, not just the top 5 most recent ones.
    - `WatchdogService` now passes the correct `currentCheckInterval` (in milliseconds) to `getRecentlyRunningAppStats`.

2.  **Foreground Service Robustness:**
    - I reviewed the existing foreground service setup, including manifest declarations (`foregroundServiceType="specialUse"`) and `NotificationHelper`. I confirmed its compatibility and robustness for Android API levels 28 through 34. No code changes were needed in this area.

3.  **Documentation & Maintainability:**
    - I added KDoc comments to `WatchdogService.kt` and `RecentAppChecker.kt` to emphasize the critical runtime permissions required for reliable operation (specifically `PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS` and `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`). This aims to improve understanding for future maintenance.

These changes should lead to more accurate detection of non-running monitored apps and improve the overall reliability of the WatchdogService as intended.

body: ### 概要 - [［作って学ぶ］OSのしくみⅠ](https://gihyo.jp/book/2025/978-4-297-14859-1)の64ページで、`locate_graphic_protocol`のライフタイムについて下記のように解説されている - > 実際にはこの関数のシグネチャ（型定義）より、このポインタのライフタイムは、引数として渡している`EfiSystemTable` の参照が持つライフタイムと同じになるとコンパイラによって推論されます[^注34]。 > [^注34]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/lifetime-elision.html - - 注34にある仕様書ではないが、[The Rust Programming Language](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch10-03-lifetime-syntax.html#lifetime-elision)の説明をまとめるとこの 👇 ようになると考えられる 1. 引数にある参照は別々のライフタイムになるので、`&EfiSystemTable`には`'a`とは別のライフタイムパラメーターがわりあてられる 2. 入力にライフタイムパラメーターがある場合はそれが返り値にも割り当てされるが、今回は`EfiGraphicsOutputProtocol`のライフタイムは明示的にライフタイムパラメーター`'a`が割り当てされていた - したがってこれまでの`locate_graphic_protocol`は下記のように引数と返り値で異なるライフタイムパラメーターが割り当てされていたと考えられる ```rust pub fn locate_graphic_protocol<'a, 'b>( efi_system_table: Pin<&'b EfiSystemTable>, ) -> Result<&'a EfiGraphicsOutputProtocol<'a>> { ``` - ☝️ このコードは`'a == 'b`なライフタイムパラメーターを取ることもできるし、または`'a != 'b`なライフタイムパラメーターを取ることもできる、より制約が少ない汎用的な関数となっていた - Playgroundででやってみても、引数と返り値のライフタイムが異っても型チェックを通過する - https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=eb74f4416e82709faf707e40d8eaf660 - 下記のコミットまでは引数`efi_system_table`も返り値も同じライフタイムパラメーター`'a`が用いられていたので、リファクタリングの際に意図せず異なるライフタイムパラメーターになってしまったと判断し、本を正としたライフタイムパラメーターに修正した - https://github.com/hikalium/wasabi/commit/9880bafcf47a58aa91c0afd02b989606e48b2865#diff-d5574fd4576a39d0ac0a2e0da032689b971a4a3ffcac06ba2f4751aeced1be48R727-R728 - Playgroundでもこちらは型が通らなくなる - https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=04753ef66bf1468b62bff947de740cf0

Current coverage is 80%. #### Proposed Changes These are the guts of the PR, and much less work than I expected: [c55dc7a...a436917](https://github.com/BrianHenryIE/Simple-PHP-Code-Parser/compare/c55dc7aad778426776a25df76c6fa806bd4a5784...a436917e6b1a86850fe070b1e923e7b0d7508afc) `php-parser` has a [UPGRADE-5.0](https://github.com/nikic/PHP-Parser/blob/master/UPGRADE-5.0.md) guide. requirements](https://github.com/nikic/PHP-Parser/blob/master/UPGRADE-5.0.md#php-version-requirements) – seems irrelevant since this library already has [a PHP 7.4 support](https://github.com/nikic/PHP-Parser/blob/master/UPGRADE-5.0.md#php-5-parsing-support) – as above, NA? * [ ] [Changes to the parser factory](https://github.com/nikic/PHP-Parser/blob/master/UPGRADE-5.0.md#changes-to-the-parser-factory) [c55dc7a Instantiate parser via `::createForNewestSupportedVersion()`](https://github.com/voku/Simple-PHP-Code-Parser/commit/c55dc7aad778426776a25df76c6fa806bd4a5784) > The createForNewestSupportedVersion() and creatForHostVersion() are available since PHP-Parser 4.18.0, to allow libraries to support PHP-Parser 4 and 5 at the same time more easily. `composer require "nikic/php-parser":"^4.18 || ^5"` (in Thanks for asking me to work on this. I will get started on it and keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress.

Original description:

> Update NanoCog checkpoint loading logic to enable adaptive attention allocation for device compatibility. Currently, checkpoint loading in sample.py and potentially train.py attempts to map to a CUDA device even when CUDA is unavailable, resulting in a RuntimeError. To ensure cognitive synergy and distributed cognition across hardware substrates, checkpoint loading must conditionally route tensors to the appropriate device (CPU if CUDA is not available).
> 
> Implementation pathway:
> - In both sample.py and train.py, replace any instance of torch.load(ckpt_path, map_location=device) or similar with logic that:
>   - Checks if torch.cuda.is_available()
>   - If CUDA is available, loads without map_location, else loads with map_location=torch.device('cpu')
> - This ensures emergent adaptability and robust operation regardless of hardware substrate.
> 
> Example replacement:
> import torch
> if torch.cuda.is_available():
>     checkpoint = torch.load(ckpt_path)
> else:
>     checkpoint = torch.load(ckpt_path, map_location=torch.device('cpu'))
> 
> Apply this pattern to all checkpoint loading code in sample.py and train.py for maximal distributed cognition and substrate-adaptive operation.

Make everything Amazing!

body:
* Accept the decimals of each reserve (`offer_dec`, `ask_dec`) and
  **up-scale the lower-decimal side to a common `target_dec`** before doing
  any math.  
  – fixes panic on pools like 6-dec vs 18-dec where `price_floor` used to
    underflow.

* Perform constant-product calculation through unchanged `compute_swap_raw`
  (still `Uint128`), but convert to `Uint256` for the up-scaled inputs so the
  multiply never overflows.

* Down-scale the three outputs (return, spread, fee) back to the ask-asset’s
  native decimals, returning the same `Uint128` API as before.

* Removes the last source of `uint256.rs: attempt to subtract with overflow`
  and guarantees every mixed-decimal pool (0–18) works without code changes
  elsewhere.

author: andrew-ting
body:
This PR replaces the universal render pipeline and all its baggage with a very barebones custom scriptable render pipeline (aka SRP) better fit to our game. It comes with a test scene so you can see how objects should now be rendered in this render pipeline.

Note that a lot of added components will not immediately render like in URP, because they get the default URP shaders on creation which are not supported in this barebones SRP. Majority of the time, the fix is to just use the new `UnlitMaterial` under `Graphics/Materials`. This shader simply receives a texture and displays it as is on the screen, which covers most use cases. If more advanced shaders are needed (for animation, lighting, etc.) we should make them as we go.

author: ktehranchi
body:
## Changes proposed in this Pull Request
- Fixes issues with RPS, TCT, REM opts when using myopic algorithm (#518) @lfreese 
- Implements a new `trim` configuration for `model_topology`: Similar to `include` (which at some point I will deprecate), Trim splits a section of a network from the core network but retains all buses one-step outside of the network. Buses at those networks are equipped with imports generators set to the marginal cost of OCGT. Emission for the imports are set according to California's imports policy since I've developed this specifically for CA.
usage example to model CA at county resolution with reeds network while modeling external WECC regions as imports :
```
model_topology:
  transmission_network: 'reeds' # [reeds, tamu]
  topological_boundaries: 'county' # [county, reeds_zone]
  interface_transmission_limits: false
  include: # mixed zone types not supported
  aggregate: # eligible keys: [reeds_zone, trans_reg]
  trim: 
    zone: ['CA']
```
- Enables `nhours` param to be used for multi-horizon networks

author: liudf0716
body:
This commit addresses two main issues:

1.  Fixes a potential buffer overflow in the `arp_get_mac` function (in `src/wd_util.c`) by replacing `strcpy` with `strncpy` when copying the device name to `arpreq.arp_dev`. Ensured null termination.

2.  Refactors the IP and MAC address retrieval logic within the `ev_http_callback_auth` function (in `src/http.c`):
    - Clarified memory management for `remote_host` and `mac` variables, ensuring `free` is called correctly before reassigning pointers when deriving IP/MAC from the connection rather than query parameters.
    - When IP/MAC are derived from the connection:
        - The client's IP is obtained via `ev_http_connection_get_peer` and duplicated using `safe_strdup`.
        - The client's MAC is obtained by calling `br_arp_get_mac` with a stack-allocated buffer, and the result is then duplicated using `safe_strdup`.
    - Added more robust error checking during this derivation process.

3.  Changed `strdup` to `safe_strdup` in `ev_http_callback_temporary_pass` for consistency when assigning a default timeout value.

author: ssk97
body:
This is a cleaned version of #11619.

This makes it so that if a permanent is entering as the ability's zcc is being updated, then the zcc is the permanent's instead of the spell's. An ability that happens "as ~ enters" will *not* have a changed zcc, as it isn't put into the entering list until after those abilities have been processed. The new `SigardasSplendorTest` verifies this behavior.

This also centralizes the updating of ability zcc, though `addDelayedTriggeredAbility` is unchanged due to to d8959f1588f0556ba4f4604d5c0dbf98350333b8. The only logic change is in the `getPermanentEntering` check.

Fixes #11728

author: copilot
body:
The continuous query was failing to process Event Hub data because it was trying to parse nested JSON fields from a string value. The `requestbody` field in the Event Hub data is a JSON string, not a parsed object, which caused JSONPath expressions like `$.properties.requestbody.Properties.PrincipalId` to fail.

## Changes Made

### 1. Fixed WHERE Clause
Changed from exact field matching to string contains matching:
```yaml
# Before (broken)
WHERE r.roleDefinitionId = '/providers/Microsoft.Authorization/roleDefinitions/1c0163c0-47e6-4577-8991-ea5c82e286e4'

# After (working)  
WHERE r.requestBody CONTAINS '1c0163c0-47e6-4577-8991-ea5c82e286e4'
```

### 2. Removed Broken JSONPath Expressions
Eliminated expressions that tried to parse JSON strings as objects:
```yaml
# These don't work because requestbody is a string, not an object
principalId: $.properties.requestbody.Properties.PrincipalId
principalType: $.properties.requestbody.Properties.PrincipalType
roleDefinitionId: $.properties.requestbody.Properties.RoleDefinitionId
```

### 3. Simplified Property Extraction
Focused on directly accessible fields from the Event Hub JSON structure:
- `callerIpAddress`, `resourceId`, `operationName`
- Identity claims for email, name, tenant ID
- Event metadata like `resultType`, `timestamp`, `location`
- Raw `requestBody` for manual parsing if needed

## Event Hub Data Structure
The Event Hub sends data like this:
```json
{
  "records": [{
    "properties": {
      "requestbody": "{\"Id\":\"...\",\"Properties\":{\"PrincipalId\":\"...\"}}"
    }
  }]
}
```

The `requestbody` is a JSON string that would need separate parsing - it's not directly accessible via JSONPath.

## Validation
- ✅ All JSONPath expressions now extract data successfully
- ✅ WHERE clause correctly identifies target role assignments  
- ✅ Middleware processes both "Start" and "Success" event types
- ✅ Configuration works with the provided Event Hub data structure

Fixes #7.

author: kedhareswer
body:
This commit introduces a comprehensive set of features to improve PDF document processing and overall application security:

1.  **Server-Side PDF Extraction:**
    *   The API route `app/api/pdf/extract/route.ts` now performs actual server-side PDF text extraction using `pdf-parse`.

2.  **Client-Side and Server-Side UI Integration:**
    *   The `components/pdf-processor.tsx` component has been refactored. It now attempts client-side PDF processing first.
    *   If client-side processing fails or is insufficient, it falls back to the server-side extraction API.

3.  **OCR for Scanned PDFs:**
    *   The server-side extraction at `app/api/pdf/extract/route.ts` is enhanced with OCR capabilities using `tesseract.js` and `pdf2pic`. This allows processing of image-based/scanned PDFs if initial text extraction by `pdf-parse` yields minimal content.

4.  **Enhanced API Key Security (OpenAI):**
    *   OpenAI API calls within `lib/ai-client.ts` are now routed through dedicated Next.js backend API routes (`app/api/openai/*`).
    *   This prevents exposure of the OpenAI API key on the client-side, significantly improving security. A similar pattern is recommended for other AI providers.

5.  **Alternative Python PDF Processing Service:**
    *   A basic Python FastAPI service for PDF text extraction using `PyPDF2` has been developed (`python_pdf_service/`).
    *   This service is containerized with a Dockerfile and provides an alternative for PDF processing if Node.js libraries have limitations. Conceptual integration with the Next.js backend is outlined.

6.  **Testing Preparation:**
    *   A detailed `E2E_TESTING_CHECKLIST.md` has been created to guide manual end-to-end testing of the new PDF processing pipeline and RAG functionality.
    *   An API test script, `api_extract_test.mjs`, has been provided for direct testing of the server-side PDF extraction endpoint.

These changes provide a more robust, secure, and versatile PDF processing pipeline, enabling more reliable data extraction for the RAG engine.

author: copilot
body:
Fixed the window condition behavior to match proper GUI drag interactions as requested in the issue.

## Problem
The window condition had two problematic behaviors:
1. **Always following cursor**: The window moved on every mouse movement, regardless of button state
2. **No proper drag behavior**: Users couldn't independently move the cursor or click to select objects

## Solution
Implemented drag-only window movement similar to the existing scroll condition:

### Key Changes
- **Event listeners**: Changed from `mousemove` to `mousedown`/`mouseup` pattern
- **Drag detection**: Window only moves when mouse button is held down (`isMouseDown` state)
- **Click vs drag**: Added drag distance tracking to distinguish clicks from drags
- **Object selection**: Clicks without significant drag (≤5px) select objects, drags >5px are ignored

### New Behavior
✅ **Mouse movement without button**: Cursor moves independently, window stays stationary  
✅ **Drag operation**: Click and hold within window area moves window with cursor  
✅ **Click without drag**: Selects objects within the window  
✅ **Click after significant drag**: Ignored to prevent accidental selection  

### Implementation Details
```javascript
// Before: Window always followed cursor
document.addEventListener('mousemove', moveWindow);

// After: Window only moves during drag
searchWindow.addEventListener('mousedown', startWindowDrag);
document.addEventListener('mousemove', dragWindow);
document.addEventListener('mouseup', endWindowDrag);
```

The `dragWindow` function now checks `isMouseDown && viewCondition === 'window'` before moving the window, ensuring it only responds during active drag operations.

### Testing
Added comprehensive tests (`test_window_fix.html`) that verify:
- No movement on mouse movement without drag
- Proper movement during drag operations  
- Object selection with small movements
- Prevention of selection after significant drags

This now behaves like standard desktop GUI drag operations (similar to moving files in a file manager).

Fixes #12.

body: Fixes a bug that caused the burst shots multiplier to not function correctly, as well as an oversight with the distance-to-target input, which needs to _not_ subtract the radius of the target ship (the way turrets do by default) or else we'll get very unintuitive behavior. Also, adds target radius as an input, which allows weapons to e.g. behave differently depending on whether they're shooting at fighters or capital ships.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>evanw/esbuild (esbuild)</summary>

### [`v0.25.5`](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0255)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/compare/v0.25.4...v0.25.5)

-   Fix a regression with `browser` in `package.json` ([#​4187](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4187))

    The fix to [#​4144](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4144) in version 0.25.3 introduced a regression that caused `browser` overrides specified in `package.json` to fail to override relative path names that end in a trailing slash. That behavior change affected the `axios@0.30.0` package. This regression has been fixed, and now has test coverage.

-   Add support for certain keywords as TypeScript tuple labels ([#​4192](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4192))

    Previously esbuild could incorrectly fail to parse certain keywords as TypeScript tuple labels that are parsed by the official TypeScript compiler if they were followed by a `?` modifier. These labels included `function`, `import`, `infer`, `new`, `readonly`, and `typeof`. With this release, these keywords will now be parsed correctly. Here's an example of some affected code:

    ```ts
    type Foo = [
      value: any,
      readonly?: boolean, // This is now parsed correctly
    ]
    ```

-   Add CSS prefixes for the `stretch` sizing value ([#​4184](https://redirect.github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/4184))

    This release adds support for prefixing CSS declarations such as `div { width: stretch }`. That CSS is now transformed into this depending on what the `--target=` setting includes:

    ```css
    div {
      width: -webkit-fill-available;
      width: -moz-available;
      width: stretch;
    }
    ```

</details>

author: avi-sanwal
body:
This is a minor improvement from security standpoint on flink's docker image.

In the dockerfile of flink's docker image, we are adding gosu:
https://github.com/apache/flink-docker/blob/6e226503dbb228467905c70ccfb6f33f4c676872/1.20/scala_2.12-java17-ubuntu/Dockerfile#L27-L44
This is later used to switch to the user flink in the entrypoint script: https://github.com/apache/flink-docker/blob/6e226503dbb228467905c70ccfb6f33f4c676872/1.20/scala_2.12-java17-ubuntu/docker-entrypoint.sh#L37.

Gosu itself is tagged by popular scanners as being vulnerable due to outdated golang usage (though gosu itself is not).

Instead of using gosu/su-exec, it may be preferrable to switch to flink user using USER flink or something similar in Dockerfile. This way we could avoid depending on gosu, and present a cleaner scan result.

While this does not really solve any vulnerabilties in the system, it can help satisfy auditors against false positive reports provided by heuristical scanners.

author: vbharath18
body:
This commit introduces a basic Flask application featuring:

- A simple chat interface (`index.html`) allowing you to send messages.
  - Frontend JavaScript handles message display and sending to the backend.
- An admin interface (`admin.html`) for managing MCP server configurations.
  - Server configurations (name, host, port) can be added via a form.
  - Configurations are stored in-memory (will reset on app restart).
  - The admin page displays the current list of configured servers.
- Backend logic (`app.py`):
  - Serves the chat and admin HTML pages.
  - Handles form submissions from the admin page to add servers.
  - Provides an endpoint (`/send_message`) for the chat interface to submit messages (currently prints to console).
- Basic MCP client structure (`mcp_client.py`) as a placeholder.
- Unit tests (`test_app.py`) for the Flask application routes and basic logic, ensuring:
  - Correct page rendering.
  - Server addition functionality and error handling in the admin section.
  - Message submission endpoint behavior.

The project structure includes templates, static files, and configuration management.

author: keito4
body:
## 概要
`src/types.ts`での型定義を厳密化し、型安全性を大幅に向上させました。

## 主な変更点

**1. 厳密な型定義**
- `SupportedType` union: `'String' | 'Number' | 'Boolean' | 'DateTime' | 'Json'`
- `NotionPropertyType` : `NotionPropertyTypes`列挙型を使用
- `FieldAttribute` union: 有効なフィールド属性

**2. ジェネリクス型の活用**
- `Field<T extends SupportedType>` インターフェース
- 型固有のインターフェース (StringField、NumberField等)
- 型ガード関数の実装

**3. 安全性の向上**
- `any`型の排除 (`Json` → `Record<string, unknown>`)
- readonly 属性配列で不変性を保証
- 包括的な型テストを追加

## 関連Issue
Closes #43

This version introduces a new CertCompressionAlgo implementation for certificateRequestMsgTLS13 in handshake_messages.go, addressing issue https://github.com/refraction-networking/utls/issues/345.

The change resolves the error: 'tls: invalid signature by the server certificate: crypto/rsa: verification error'

author: parsaa74
body:
Umfeld doesn't work on Arch Linux out of the box - cmake breaks and harfbuzz linking fails. 

Fixed both issues by adding an install script that handles all the arch-specific twists. CMake sometimes can't find its modules so I made a wrapper script. Also harfbuzz's cmake config is broken on arch so switched to pkg-config instead.

Tested on my arch system and now everything builds fine. Should help other arch users.

Changes:
- install-arch.sh (handles dependencies + fixes)
- cmake_wrapper.sh (fixes cmake issues)  
- CMakeLists.txt (use pkg-config for harfbuzz)

body:
This pull request introduces several updates to the project, including dependency additions, UI enhancements, and codebase modifications. Key changes include adding new dependencies, updating branding assets, enhancing the dashboard component with a responsive mobile menu and logout functionality, and removing unused routes and components.

### Dependency Updates:
* Added new dependencies to `package.json` and `web/package-lock.json`, including `react-icons`, `@tabler/icons-react`, `clsx`, `motion`, `ogl`, `react-dropzone`, and `tailwind-merge`. These libraries provide functionality for icons, animations, file handling, and utility classes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R1-R5) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3ebf69f247f3231fd796e60555489b4a1ed684e3ad4cb0ace460a2ed07d53a95R11-R32) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b861012a5dd72b8a9f3281b7cf09f5a779c98569d040b1bbc1db50f1b15e7cceR6-R27)

### Branding and UI Enhancements:
* Updated the favicon, Apple touch icon, and meta description in `web/public/index.html` to reflect the branding of "SoDA Admin." Added preconnect links for Google Fonts and included the "JetBrains Mono" font. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c7b50ecbd6d7e2b1668240bb06ba860f904a74df93c9aaa9bb1f6f1c2608ee5dL5-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c7b50ecbd6d7e2b1668240bb06ba860f904a74df93c9aaa9bb1f6f1c2608ee5dL27-R30)
* Updated `web/public/manifest.json` to include new branding assets and change the app's name and theme color.

### Dashboard Component Improvements:
* Enhanced `web/src/components/DashBoard.js` by adding a responsive mobile menu, logout functionality, and new navigation options. Integrated `react-icons` for visual elements like menu toggles and logout icons. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-57b9639cf9ab9b781d8d0f7ed6244a5c15559b4c6d28911721afcd1a02d90664L1-R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-57b9639cf9ab9b781d8d0f7ed6244a5c15559b4c6d28911721afcd1a02d90664L20-L27)

### Code Cleanup:
* Removed the unused `CreateUserPage` route and import from `web/src/App.js` to simplify the codebase. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a7af1546332212366a5170b006dcd3ebf05e77f7ccc22b3d5da8b28a09083910L20) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a7af1546332212366a5170b006dcd3ebf05e77f7ccc22b3d5da8b28a09083910L38)

body: **Package Upgrades:** * `keccak-hash`: `0.5` -> `0.11.0` * `rlp`: `0.4` -> `0.6.1`(Use forked version) * `ethereum-types`: `0.9` -> `0.15.1` ** Changes ** [parity-common/uint CHANGELOG#0.10.0](https://github.com/paritytech/parity-common/blob/f0dade11ac0b2450e6a54f36035f74b2b8ce4c00/uint/CHANGELOG.md#0100---2024-09-11) * The function `to_big_endian` has been renamed to `write_as_big_endian`. * The function `to_little_endian` has been renamed to `write_as_little_endian`. * Usage of `drain()` has been replaced with `as_raw()`. * Usage of `as_slice()` has been replaced with `as_ref()`. * The conversion `sig.r().into()` has been updated to `U256::from_big_endian(sig.r())` for explicit construction from big-endian bytes. * Updated the buffer type in `push_msg_id_leb128_encoding` from `Vec` to `BytesMut`. - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/Conflux-Chain/conflux-rust/3247) resolve #3239 ~~BREAKING CHANGE:~~ ~~The upgrade to rlp 0.6.1 :~~ ~~Previous behavior:~~ ~~True was often encoded as RLP 0x01.~~ ~~False was often encoded as RLP 0x00.~~ ~~New behavior:~~ ~~True is encoded as RLP 0x01.~~ ~~False is encoded as RLP 0x80 (representing an empty byte string).~~ ~~You can see the RLP change here : `https://github.com/paritytech/parity-common/pull/572`~~

author: rafeyrana
body:
This commit addresses several areas in the frontend to improve code clarity, modularity, and reduce prop drilling.

Key changes include:

1.  **HomePage.tsx**: Removed unused 'oldUser' state and associated conditional rendering, simplifying the component. Also removed the 'userEmail' variable which was no longer needed.

2.  **ChatBot.tsx**: Refactored to retrieve 'userEmail' directly from the Redux store instead of receiving it as a prop. This reduces prop drilling from parent components.

3.  **DocumentChat.tsx & PDFViewer.tsx**: Removed an unused text selection feature. This involved deleting the 'selectedText' state and 'handleTextSelect' function in DocumentChat.tsx, and removing the 'onTextSelect' prop and related state from PDFViewer.tsx.

4.  **DocumentChat.tsx**: Updated to no longer pass 'userEmail' to ChatBot.tsx, as ChatBot now sources this data from Redux. Consequently, the 'userEmail' variable and its import were removed from DocumentChat.tsx.

These changes contribute to a cleaner, more maintainable, and extensible frontend codebase.

author: sahil-u07
body:
Closes #4

## Overview
This PR adds a one‐time, character‐by‐character typing animation to the landing page headline:

**The AI Marketplace For Next-Gen Solutions**

Previously, the headline was static. Now, on page load, each character types in at 100 ms intervals, with a CSS‐driven blinking cursor. Once the full text appears, the cursor disappears.

---

## Key Details

- **Typing Behavior**
  - Characters appear at 100 ms per character.
  - The substring “AI Marketplace” (indices 4–17) renders in the accent teal color (`colors.accent[500]`); all other characters render in white.
  - A blinking cursor (`.animate-blink`) appears during typing and stops once the headline is fully displayed.

- **Responsiveness & Performance**
  - Uses Tailwind’s `text-4xl md:text-5xl lg:text-6xl` and `leading-tight` for smooth scaling on mobile, tablet, and desktop.
  - Renders transparent non‐breaking spaces (`'\u00A0'`) for characters not yet typed to reserve each “slot,” preventing any layout shift.
  - Runs only once on page load (no looping), minimizing CPU usage.

- **Implementation Highlights**
  1. **State**
     - `visibleCount` (number of characters currently typed)
     - `typingComplete` (boolean to stop the interval and hide the cursor)
  2. **Effect**
     - On mount, a `setInterval` increments `visibleCount` by 1 every 100 ms until it reaches the full headline length. Then it clears itself and sets `typingComplete = true`.
  3. **Rendering**
     - In `<h1>`, iterate over `fullText.split('')`:
       - If `i < visibleCount`, render the actual character in its final color (teal for “AI Marketplace,” white otherwise).
       - Else, render a transparent non‐breaking space (`'\u00A0'`) to reserve that slot.
     - Show `<span className="inline-block w-[2px] bg-current ml-1 animate-blink" />` until `typingComplete` is `true`.
  4. **CSS**
     - Added:
       ```css
       @keyframes blink {
         0%, 49%  { opacity: 1; }
         50%, 99% { opacity: 0; }
         100%     { opacity: 1; }
       }
       .animate-blink {
         animation: blink 1s step-start infinite;
       }
       ```
     - This ensures the cursor blinks via CSS rather than React state updates.

---

author: derekbreden
body:
The comment in `client/testHelpers.js` regarding the origin of the Mock DOM helper functions (`createMockElement`, `createMockDocument`, `createMockWindow`) was outdated.

These functions are now canonical in `client/testHelpers.js`, and `flint.test.js` (the referenced original source) consumes them from this file.

The comment has been updated from:
`// Mock DOM Implementation (copied and adapted from flint.test.js)` to:
`// Mock DOM Implementation`

This change improves clarity about the source of these utilities and is a small step towards better consistency in test mocking. No functional code was changed, and all tests continue to pass.

author: seocylucky
body:
## 🔥 Related Issues

- close #64 

## 💜 작업 내용

- [x] 날짜 선택 UI 작업
- [x] 카테고리별 소비통계 조회 API 연동 `/api/statistics/consumption-statistic`
- [x] 소비 습관 개선 리포트 조회 API 연동 `/api/reports/consumption-report`

## ✅ PR Point

- 공통 컴포넌트인 BottomSheet를 이용하여 날짜별 선택 바텀시트를 만들었습니다. 배경을 클릭 시, 닫힐 수 있도록 onClose 옵셔널 속성을 초가하였습니다.
- 월별 선택에 따라 리포트 요약과 카테고리별 소비 통계를 동적으로 조회할 수 있도록 구성했습니다.
- useAvailableConsumptionMonth, useConsumptionReport, useConsumptionStatistic 세 가지 커스텀 훅을 작성하여 각각의 API 응답을 모듈화하고, Query Key와 enabled 옵션을 통해 조건부 패칭이 가능하도록 처리했습니다.
- 최대 3개의 카테고리만 띄울 수 있게 해놓았으며, 현재 각각의 위치는 고정 위치입니다.

## 😡 Trouble Shooting

### useState 초기값에서 months runtime 에러
useState 초기값에서 months가 undefined일 수 있어 runtime 에러가 발생했었습니다.
```tsx
const { data: months } = useAvailableConsumptionMonth(token);
const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState(() => {
  const [year, month] = months[0].split('-'); // 🚨
  return { year, month };
});
```
useMemo를 활용해 months가 있을때만 안전하게 초기값을 만들 수 있도록 하였습니다.
```tsx
const initialDate = useMemo(() => {
  if (!months || months.length === 0) return null;
  const [year, month] = months[0].split('-');
  return { year, month };
}, [months]);

```

### React Hook must be called in the same order 에러
조건부를 활용해 커스텀 훅 호출을 부를려 했지만 이는 리액트 규칙 위반인 것을 알았습니다.
어떻게 이 초기 상태값이 있을 때만 훅을 호출할 수 있게 할지 고민하다가 커스텀 훅의 enabled를 활용하여 조건부 호출을 할 수 있도록 하였습니다.
[관련문서](https://legacy.reactjs.org/docs/hooks-rules.html)
```tsx
const { data: reports } = useConsumptionReport(token, yearMonth, !!initialDate);
```

### 데이터 바뀔 때마다 애니메이션 동작
날짜 데이터가 바뀔 때마다 애니메이션이 동작할 수 있도록 motion 컴포넌트에 월별데이터 key값을 주어 애니메이션이 동작하도록 하였습니다.
```tsx
<CircleContainer key={yearMonth}>
  {topStats.map(...)}
</CircleContainer>
```

author: phoeagon
body:
(Hi this is the original author, phoeagon)

updated the Chinese translation file. I did some spot check on the app loading up the example files and confirms that it works.

There are a few places where I don't see translation labels available in the file.
For example "struct" is C doesn't appear to be translatable. "Default" as in "default value" of parameter/argument of the function dialog is also not translatable. Also for C/C++ programs "Ref" (probably referring to whether passing by value or reference) is also not translatable.

As is consistent with current translation, it uses Simplified Chinese characters and vocabulary. Users from HK/TW may not be particularly familiar with these.

author: glepnir
body:
Problem:
- nvim_parse_cmd('copen', {}) returns count: 0, causing nvim_cmd to override default behavior
- nvim_cmd({cmd = 'copen', args = {10}}, {}) fails with "Wrong number of arguments"

Solution:
- Only include count field in parse result when explicitly provided or non-zero
- Interpret single numeric argument as count for count-only commands like copen

Fix #21313
Fix #23121

body:
Основные изменения:
Анализ дубликатов:
Добавлен режим --deep-duplicates any-name для поиска дубликатов по телу функции независимо от имени (AST-хеш).
Флаг --no-prod-filter позволяет видеть дубликаты даже если они только в архиве/тестах.
Фильтрация production-дубликатов теперь прозрачна: статус фильтра явно указывается в отчёте.
Улучшена документация по анализу дубликатов, фильтрации и best practices.
CLI и парсер:
Поддержка строгой фильтрации по директориям: --include-dir, --exclude-dir.
Улучшена обработка паттернов, нормализация директорий.
Все новые опции отражены в справке и документации.
Модульный индекс:
Новый флаг --modular-index для команды parse — создаёт .llmstruct_index/ с отдельными struct.json и ast.json для каждого файла/модуля.
Структура папки повторяет структуру исходного кода.
В .gitignore добавлено правило для игнорирования .llmstruct_*.
Документация:
Обновлён docs/cli.md: подробно описаны новые режимы анализа, фильтрация, модульный индекс, рекомендации по использованию.
В папку TODO добавлена заметка о необходимости fallback-анализа, если в struct.json нет исходников функций, и идеи по развитию модульного индекса.
UX и прозрачность:
Везде добавлены предупреждения и пояснения для пользователя (например, если struct.json не содержит исходников).
Все новые опции CLI снабжены подробным help.
Список коммитов (с кратким описанием):
feat(duplication): add --deep-duplicates any-name mode for cross-name function body deduplication
Новый режим поиска дубликатов по телу функции независимо от имени.
Улучшена фильтрация production/test/archive.
Документация и UX обновлены.
feat: add --no-prod-filter to show all duplicates including archive/tests
Флаг для отключения фильтрации production-дубликатов.
Статус фильтра явно отражён в отчёте и CLI.
docs: update CLI documentation for new duplicate analysis and filtering
Подробное описание новых опций, best practices, примеры.
feat(index): modular .llmstruct_index/ for per-module struct/ast analysis
Флаг --modular-index для генерации модульного индекса.
Пример структуры, обновление .gitignore.
docs: add TODO for fallback analysis and modular index ideas
TODO/ast_fallback.md с идеями по развитию архитектуры анализа.
Как тестировать:
Ознакомьтесь с обновлённой справкой CLI (--help) и документацией (docs/cli.md).
Проверьте работу новых режимов анализа дубликатов:
--deep-duplicates same-name (по умолчанию)
--deep-duplicates any-name
--no-prod-filter
Сгенерируйте модульный индекс:
Apply to validate_ses...
Run
Проверьте структуру .llmstruct_index/.
Убедитесь, что .llmstruct_* не попадает в git.
Важно
BREAKING: Аргумент --deep-duplicates теперь требует значения (same-name или any-name), старый булевый флаг не поддерживается.
Для глубокого анализа рекомендуется использовать модульный индекс.
Готово к ревью и обсуждению!

## About The Pull Request

I really dislike the combat_bog track, being just a ten second loop of what sounds like pots and pans clanging together... So, this PR adds combat_vanguard.ogg and gives it to Vanguards and Wardens. Also adds it to credits.txt....

<!-- Describe The Pull Request. Please be sure every change is documented or this can delay review and even discourage maintainers from merging your PR! -->

## Why It's Good For The Game

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZH5eHnLGRP8

The track is Felvidék from a game of the same name. It's meant to be heroic at its core but is somehow offputting and vaguely depressing, to mirror the main character, Pavol, who is a slovakian veteran suffering from alcoholism after giving in to the trauma of almost losing his life in Kosovo. Despite this, he always carries a shit-eating grin and jokes around, knowing that the show must go on. Personally I found it fitting! All of it gives it a laugh in the face of death feeling.

While the BPM on it is on the lower end, I thought that it would still work fine, especially with how there's a few other tracks that are a bit slower and heavier, like werewolf or brigand. Talking to a few other vanguard players on discord, i got positive responses on the choice.

Potential fix for [https://github.com/slowedcodinganai/kubernetes/security/code-scanning/13](https://github.com/slowedcodinganai/kubernetes/security/code-scanning/13)

To fix the issue, we need to validate the `header.Name` and the resulting `destFileName.String()` to ensure they do not contain unsafe path components. Specifically:
1. Strip any `..` sequences and ensure the path is relative to the intended destination directory.
2. Use `filepath.Clean` to normalize the path and check that it does not escape the target directory.
3. Reject paths that are absolute or contain invalid components.

The fix involves modifying the code in `staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/cp/cp.go` to include these validations before using the path in file operations.

body:
**User Functionality & Navigation
MF Suites Hotel Reservation System
Branch: user**


**What is the User Branch?**
The user branch is dedicated to all features, pages, and components that serve the hotel’s guests. It provides a seamless, user-friendly interface for guests to manage their entire hotel experience—from browsing rooms to booking, payments, and account management.

**Key Features of the User Branch**

**Authentication & Profile**

- Register: Create a new guest account.
- Login/Logout: Securely access and exit the system.
- Forgot/Reset Password: Recover account access if needed.
- Profile Management: View and update personal details, upload a profile picture, and manage payment accounts.
- Account Deletion: Option to permanently delete the user account.

**Room Browsing & Booking**

- Browse Rooms: View all available room types with images, descriptions, and included services.
- Book Rooms: Select dates, services, and payment method to make a reservation.
- Real-Time Availability: Check if rooms are available for selected dates.

**Reservations Management**

- View Reservations: See all current, past, and cancelled bookings.
- Reservation Details: View full details of each booking, including payment and services.
- Cancel Reservations: Request cancellation and see status updates.
- Trash/Restore: Hide or restore deleted reservations for better organization.
- 

**Notifications**

- Notification Bell: See a badge for unread notifications (e.g., booking status, admin actions).
- Notification Center: View all notifications, mark as read, and delete as needed.

**Wallet & Payments**

- Wallet System: Top up wallet for quick payments and receive refunds.
- Multiple Payment Methods: GCash, Bank, PayPal, Credit Card, and Wallet.
- Transaction History: View all wallet transactions.

**Settings & Preferences**

- Change Password: Update account security.
- Theme Switcher: Toggle between light and dark mode, with persistent preference.
- Payment Info: Manage and update payment accounts.

**UI/UX**

- Responsive Design: Works on desktop, tablet, and mobile.
- Modern Navigation: Sidebar and top navigation for easy access to all features.
- Accessible Forms & Modals: User-friendly and accessible for all guests.
- Consistent Theming: Light/dark mode support across all pages.

**Other Pages**

- About: Learn about the hotel, team, and developer.
- Privacy Policy: Understand how user data is handled.
- 

**User Navigation**
The user navigation includes:

- Profile
- Rooms
- My Reservations
- Notifications
- Settings
- About
- Privacy
- Logout

This navigation is always available, making it easy for users to move between sections.

**Security**

- Session Management: Ensures only logged-in users can access their data.
- Input Validation: All forms use validation and secure database queries.
- Password Security: Passwords are stored securely and can be reset by the user.

**Summary Table**
| Feature | Description |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Register/Login | Create and access a guest account |
| Profile | View/update info, upload photo, delete account |
| Room Booking | Browse/book rooms, select services, check availability |
| Reservations | View/manage/cancel bookings, trash/restore |
| Notifications | Real-time alerts, unread badge, mark as read |
| Wallet/Payments | Top-up, refund, multiple payment methods, transaction history |
| Settings | Change password, payment info, theme preference |
| UI/UX | Responsive, modern, light/dark mode, accessible |
| Info Pages | About, Privacy |

**In summary:**
The user branch provides a complete, modern, and secure experience for hotel guests, allowing them to manage every aspect of their stay and account with ease.

author: yurisldk
body:
## Summary

This MR introduces a standardized Git-based workflow for linting, formatting, and testing to improve code consistency and prevent regressions.

Fixes: #22 

## Changes

- Added Husky pre-commit and pre-push Git hooks
  - `pre-commit`: runs ESLint and Prettier via lint-staged on staged files
  - `pre-push`: runs `yarn test` before pushing code
- Simplified ESLint script to support staged file linting correctly
- Updated `lint-staged` configuration for broad coverage of source and config files
- Reformatted the entire codebase using Prettier and ESLint
- Introduced `.git-blame-ignore-revs` with formatting commit hash to reduce noise in `git blame`

## Motivation

This setup helps:
- Enforce consistent code style across the team
- Catch lint and test issues early via Git hooks
- Keep commit history and `git blame` clean and focused on logic changes

## Post-Merge Note

To apply blame-ignore locally:

```bash
git config blame.ignoreRevsFile .git-blame-ignore-revs

body:
This pull request introduces several changes across multiple domains, focusing on improving entity creation, adding new use cases, and refining error handling. Key updates include making entity IDs optional for creation, implementing new use cases for user management, and enhancing error validation and testing.

### Entity Creation Updates:
* Made IDs optional for creation in entities like `Booking`, `Payment`, `Room`, and `User`. If not provided, IDs are now generated automatically. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-addee39a17f385a617aa0d8a1d375f19722335e18646e07880bf1fcf3a228718L29-R29)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b57ee6e434f57c2785196194114e265a6c3f8060d2849c303099525be7de98d1L31-R31)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-865a8a460dc86bf88e967660a970c7925db1723a421d90ef65085fe9a4edd9d4L27-R27)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0756b8c187c0f9151829b8389a6b796b2ff2a20a22a13b574d7aaee25d721460L27-R27)`)
* Updated constructors and static creation methods to handle optional IDs and generate them when necessary. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-addee39a17f385a617aa0d8a1d375f19722335e18646e07880bf1fcf3a228718R65-R67)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b57ee6e434f57c2785196194114e265a6c3f8060d2849c303099525be7de98d1L61-R85)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-865a8a460dc86bf88e967660a970c7925db1723a421d90ef65085fe9a4edd9d4L64-R65)`, `[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0756b8c187c0f9151829b8389a6b796b2ff2a20a22a13b574d7aaee25d721460L60-R61)`)

* Added `RegisterUserUseCase` to handle user registration with validations for email uniqueness and password strength. (`[packages/core/src/users/application/use-cases/register-user.usecase.tsR1-R60](diffhunk://#diff-90caa60ec4f4e11a3194a8380ce4bf0db0c6b38f45395c93355e3a0a3fdae223R1-R60)`)
* Added `GetUserByIdUseCase` to retrieve user details by ID, with error handling for invalid or non-existent IDs. (`[packages/core/src/users/application/use-cases/get-user-by-id.usecase.tsR1-R27](diffhunk://#diff-b017a023ff1747bef7b0f1a8df826212cd308529a394755f8c04f6dd490bbe58R1-R27)`)

### Error Handling Enhancements:

### Testing Improvements:
* Added comprehensive unit tests for the new use cases (`RegisterUserUseCase` and `GetUserByIdUseCase`) to verify behavior under various scenarios, including success and error cases. ## 📋 PR Description

This PR restructures the abstract service classes and their API implementations to follow the OrderService pattern by consolidating multiple separate abstract classes into single unified classes per domain. The changes focus on discount services (DiscountCodeService, PriceRuleService), AbandonedCheckoutsService, DraftOrderService, OrderRiskService OrderService, RefundService and TransactionService. Additionally, dependency injection has been updated to use GetIt instead of Dio for service registration.

- ✅ **Refactored folder and file names for GET operations** in the following services:
  - `DiscountCodeService`
  - `PriceRuleService`
  - `AbandonedCheckoutsService`
  - `DraftOrderService`
  - `OrderRiskService`
  - `OrderService`
  - `RefundService`
  - `TransactionService`

- 📁 **Renamed service files** to follow a consistent and clearer naming convention (e.g., `get_*.dart` → `retrieve*.dart`).

author: nbittich
body:
Antwerp should only have around  ~7500~ (edit: probably more) pages to scrape. However, the last time I checked, there were over 500k pages.

I believe the reason for this is that Antwerp adds a dynamic ;jsessionid segment to their urls. When we follow these links, the scraper adds automatically the dynamic jsessionid in its list of visited urls. This results in many variations of the same URL being treated as different pages, potentially creating a crawl loop.

This PR should resolve the issue, as it ensures we clean the url before following it.

author: odaysec
body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/002faa6baab355dbec875aeaa43e8f0fab5d9d49/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/cp/cp.go#L558-L558

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/002faa6baab355dbec875aeaa43e8f0fab5d9d49/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/cp/filespec.go#L64-L64

Fix the issue need to validate the `header.Name` and the resulting `destFileName.String()` to ensure they do not contain unsafe path components. Specifically:
1. Strip any `..` sequences and ensure the path is relative to the intended destination directory.
2. Use `filepath.Clean` to normalize the path and check that it does not escape the target directory.
3. Reject paths that are absolute or contain invalid components.

The fix involves modifying the code in `staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/cp/cp.go` to include these validations before using the path in file operations.


Accessing files using paths constructed from user-controlled data can allow an attacker to access unexpected resources. This can result in sensitive information being revealed or deleted, or an attacker being able to influence behavior by modifying unexpected files. Paths that are naively constructed from data controlled by a user may be absolute paths, or may contain unexpected special characters such as "`..`"`.` Such a path could point anywhere on the file system.

Your Custom Integration is working floorlessly on my Alira X with 3.6.0 firmware, thank you!

The DaikinEnergyTodaySensor was not appearing under **Energy → Individual devices** in Home Assistant because it lacked the proper unit, device_class, and state_class. This pull request makes the minimal changes needed so that “Daikin Energy Today” can be selected in the Energy dashboard.

self._attr_native_unit_of_measurement = UnitOfEnergy.WATT_HOUR
self._attr_device_class = SensorDeviceClass.ENERGY
self._attr_state_class = SensorStateClass.TOTAL_INCREASING
This tells HA that the sensor represents “today’s energy” (which only increases until reset), allowing it to be picked under Individual devices.

The screenshot is not showing much energy against the AliraX yet as it is only calculating the energy consumed since enabling the individual device.

author: heeyyeon
body:
## 📌 가장 고민한 문제

- 문제 링크: [단지번호붙이기](https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/2667)

---
## 💭 문제 설명
- 정사각형 형태의 지도에서 1은 집이 있는 곳, 0은 집이 없는 곳을 의미한다.
- 상하좌우로 연결된 집들이 모이면 하나의 단지로 간주한다.
- 목표: 지도를 보고 총 단지 수와, 각 단지에 속한 집의 수를 오름차순으로 출력하기
---
## 💡 해결 접근 방식

1. 2차원 배열을 탐색하면서, 1인 지점에서 DFS를 수행해 연결된 집을 하나의 단지로 묶음
2. 방문한 집은 0으로 바꾸거나 visited 배열에 체크하여 중복 탐색을 방지
3. 단지가 생길 때마다 카운트하여, 단지 수와 단지별 집의 개수 저장
---

## 🧠 사용한 개념 & 자료구조

- DFS: 어떤 집(1)을 발견하면, 연결된 모든 집을 한 번에 재귀로 방문하면서 집의 개수를 카운트 함
- 2차원 배열 탐색
```
// 상, 하, 좌, 우 방향을 탐색하기 위한 벡터
const dx = [-1, 1, 0, 0];
const dy = [0, 0, -1, 1];
```

---

## ✅ 포인트

- visited[x][y] = true: 방문한 집은 다시 탐색하지 않도록 처리
- 집의 위치마다 DFS를 시작하되, 이미 방문한 곳은 제외하기
- DFS 탐색 중 방문한 집의 수를 세어 각 단지의 집 수로 저장
- 단지 수는 DFS가 수행된 횟수, 집 수는 DFS 내에서 계산된 값
```
console.log(result.length); // 단지 수
result.sort((a, b) => a - b); // 집 수 오름차순
result.forEach(cnt => console.log(cnt)); // 각 단지별 집 수 출력
```

---

## 📚 참고자료

- (선택 사항) 참고한 블로그나 공식 문서

body:
This PR addresses the translation consistency issues reported in the Thai issue by implementing three key enhancements:

## 🎯 Features Implemented

### 1. Configurable Capture Delay (ปรับระยะเวลาการจับข้อความ)
- Added UI slider control allowing users to adjust capture interval from 0.5 to 10 seconds
- Real-time adjustment while capturing is active
- Default remains at 2 seconds with configurable min/max limits
- Status display shows current capture interval

```python
# New config options in config.py
UI_CONFIG = {
    'capture_interval': 2000,      # Default 2 seconds
    'capture_interval_min': 500,   # Minimum 0.5 seconds  
    'capture_interval_max': 10000, # Maximum 10 seconds
}
```

### 2. Translation Cache to Avoid Duplicate Ollama Calls (หลีกเลี่ยงการส่งข้อความซ้ำ)
- Implemented MD5-based caching system in `OllamaTranslator`
- Prevents redundant API calls for identical text (case-insensitive)
- Configurable cache size (default: 100 translations)
- Cache results marked with `from_cache` flag for transparency

```python
# Cache behavior example
translator = OllamaTranslator()
result1 = translator.translate("Hello World")  # API call
result2 = translator.translate("hello world")  # From cache
assert result2['from_cache'] == True
```

### 3. Game-Optimized Translation Prompt (ปรับปรุง prompt สำหรับเกม)
- Enhanced prompt specifically designed for gaming content and UI elements
- Preserves common game terms (HP, MP, Level, Boss, Guild, Quest) in English
- Better handling of game actions using appropriate Thai gaming terminology
- Maintains engaging tone suitable for Thai gamers

```python
# Game-specific translation rules
- UI elements: Save/บันทึก, Load/โหลด, Settings/ตั้งค่า
- Game actions: Attack/โจมตี, Defend/ป้องกัน, Use Skill/ใช้สกิล
- Stats: Keep "HP", "MP", "XP" in English as commonly used
```

## 🧪 Testing
- ✅ All configuration changes load correctly
- ✅ Cache system prevents duplicate API calls
- ✅ Game-specific prompts generated with appropriate context
- ✅ UI controls integrate seamlessly with existing interface
- ✅ Minimal code changes (114 additions, 22 deletions across 3 files)

## 📂 Files Modified
- `src/config.py`: Added capture interval and cache configuration
- `src/gui/window.py`: Added interval control slider and real-time adjustment
- `src/translation/ollama_translator.py`: Implemented cache system and game-optimized prompts

This enhancement improves translation consistency for gaming applications while providing users with better control over capture timing and reducing unnecessary API usage.

Fixes #9.

author: khazp
body:
feat: Implement Semantic Content Engine (Phase 1)

This commit introduces the first phase of the Semantic Content Engine for AutoTidy.

Key changes and features implemented:

1.  **Semantic Analysis (`semantic_analyzer.py`):**
    *   Integrated `python-magic` for basic MIME type detection.
    *   Integrated `tika` for text extraction from documents (PDF, DOCX, etc.).
    *   Integrated `opencv-python-headless` for basic image analysis (dimensions, average color).
    *   Integrated `ffmpeg-python` for media metadata extraction (video/audio properties, format tags).
    *   Added `generate_tags` function to create descriptive tags based on the analyzed content (MIME type, keywords from text, image properties, media metadata).

2.  **Configuration Management (`config_manager.py`):**
    *   Overhauled the rule structure to be more flexible. Folders now have a list of rules.
    *   Each rule consists of multiple `conditions` (targeting file age, filename pattern, MIME type, or tags) and `condition_logic` ('AND'/'OR').
    *   Introduced configuration versioning (`CONFIG_VERSION = "2.0.0"`). Old configurations are not automatically migrated.
    *   Added backend methods for managing new rules (add, update, remove), though UI for this is not yet implemented.

3.  **File Checking Logic (`utils.check_file`):**
    *   Significantly refactored to evaluate files against the new complex rule structure, including conditions based on semantic information (MIME types, tags).

4.  **File Processing (`utils.process_file_action`):**
    *   Enhanced to support a `{TAGS}` placeholder in the `archive_path_template`, allowing for dynamic folder creation based on generated tags.
    *   Updated history logging to include the name of the matched rule.

5.  **Core Logic (`worker.py`):**
    *   I modified the core logic to orchestrate the semantic analysis for each file.
    *   I pass semantic information (MIME type, tags, extracted text/features/metadata) to the rule checking and file processing functions.

6.  **Unit Tests (`tests/`):**
    *   Added comprehensive unit tests for `semantic_analyzer.py` and `utils.py`.
    *   All unit tests are currently passing after resolving issues with mock setups for `Path.stat` in `TestCheckFile`.

**Current Status and Next Steps:**
This implementation provides a robust backend for content-aware file processing.
The immediate next steps originally planned were:
    *   Updating `ui_config_window.py` to allow you to create and manage these new semantic rules.
    *   Updating documentation (`README.md`).

**Issue Encountered During Development:**
A significant challenge was encountered with 4 unit tests for `utils.check_file` which were persistently failing. The issue was traced to the mocking strategy for `Path.stat()` within the test environment. This was resolved by adjusting how `MagicMock` instances for `Path` objects were configured in the test `setUp` method.

All processing is designed to happen locally, preserving your privacy.

### **User description** This commit introduces a comprehensive development environment setup using Docker and a dedicated initialization script, significantly streamlining the development process for the Veridis protocol. - **Docker Environment:** - Adds a `docker/cairo/dev.Dockerfile` to create a complete Cairo development environment with Rust, Scarb, Starknet Foundry, Node.js, Python, and essential development tools. - Introduces `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` and `.devcontainer/docker-compose.yml` for VS Code devcontainer integration, enabling a consistent and reproducible development environment. - Configures persistent caches for Cairo, Scarb, Node.js modules, and contract builds to improve build times. - Sets up a non-root user (`vscode`) within the container for enhanced security. - Includes health checks to ensure all essential development tools are functioning correctly. - **Initialization Script:** - Adds `scripts/init-veridis-env.sh` to automate the setup of the Veridis development environment, including: - Installing root project dependencies. - Setting up the Cairo contracts environment. - Configuring the ZK circuits environment. - Initializing microservices (identity, attestation, verification, compliance, and bridge services). - Setting up client SDKs (TypeScript, Python, and Mobile). - Optionally configuring formal verification, GDPR compliance, and security scanning based on environment variables. - Provides clear instructions and useful commands for developers to get started. author: joecorall
body:
Reverts Islandora/chullo#101, which introduced streaming responses from fedora.

I began troubleshooting an image upload error caused by streaming our response from fedora in https://github.com/Islandora/chullo/pull/102. That caused more research to resolve the issue, and I discovered the underlying issue's resolution is spread across multiple libraries, some of which are in the core php source. Given the scope of the problem I determined we should not be attempting to reap the performance benefits of streaming http requests from fedora until the programming language and libraries we rely on provide better streaming support.

The long and short of the problem is flysystem is an abstraction for a traditional filesystem. Some core php functions (e.g. [imagesize](https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.getimagesize.php)) and/or php libraries assume seekable streams (i.e. you can move a pointer back and forth for a file being read). Since our flysystem integration with fedora is over http, if we stream the fedora response that stream is not seekable since http can only be read once. This causes any function call assuming seekable streams to throw errors.

Some example issues covering the scope of the problem:

https://bugs.php.net/bug.php?id=69706
https://github.com/guzzle/psr7/issues/535
https://github.com/thephpleague/flysystem/issues/419
https://github.com/thephpleague/flysystem/issues/1579
https://www.drupal.org/project/flysystem_s3/issues/3203286

CC @rbos

This pull request updates the CodeQL workflow to improve automation and adds new configurations for building and publishing Electron packages. It also includes dependency updates in `package.json` to align with the project requirements.

### Workflow Improvements

* Updated `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` to trigger builds only on tag pushes (e.g., `v1.2.3`) instead of all pushes to the `main` branch, reducing unnecessary releases.

* Modified the build step to use `npm run build:ci` for CI-specific builds, and added a new step to publish Electron packages when a tag is pushed. This step generates `.AppImage`, `.deb`, and other artifacts using `electron-builder`.

* Downgraded `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin` and `@typescript-eslint/parser` from `^8.30.1` to `^7.0.0`.

This commit includes the foundational setup for the backend of the educational assistant platform.

Key features implemented:
1.  **Project Initialization:** Node.js/Express project with TypeScript.

10. **Error Handling:** Implemented global error handling middleware and a 404 Not Found handler.

The backend is now structured with core functionalities for content ingestion and processing, along with placeholders for AI features and a database connection.

author: rakeshnreddy
body:
Corrected a `jinja2.exceptions.UndefinedError` that occurred in `templates/index.html`. The error was due to an incorrect method of accessing dynamically named template context variables (previously trying `_context`, which was undefined).

The fix involves:
- Modified `templates/index.html`:
  - In the loop for period inputs (`period<k>_duration`, `period<k>_r`, `period<k>_i`), changed the `value` attributes.
  - Replaced expressions like `value="{{ request.form.get('key') or _context['key'] }}"` with `value="{{ request.form.get('key') or vars()['key'] }}"`.
  - This uses Jinja's `vars()` function, which provides access to a dictionary of the current template variables, allowing for dynamic key access.

This ensures that default values for form fields are accessed using a standard and reliable Jinja mechanism, resolving the `UndefinedError`.

author: denovo1998
body:
### Motivation

In modern event-driven architectures, the ability to react to changing conditions is crucial. While Pulsar's delayed message feature is valuable for scheduling future tasks or deliveries, the lack of a cancellation mechanism presents a limitation. Use cases where cancellation is important include:

- An order is placed with delayed processing, but the user cancels the order before processing begins.
- A scheduled notification becomes obsolete due to a subsequent user action.
- System alerts scheduled for future delivery are resolved before the delivery time.

Without a cancellation feature, applications might resort to workarounds, such as:

- Consumers receiving and then filtering/ignoring obsolete delayed messages, which wastes processing resources and bandwidth.
- Maintaining complex state management on the client-side to track and ignore messages, which is error-prone and doesn't prevent the message from being delivered by the broker.

This proposal aims to introduce a robust mechanism to cancel delayed messages directly at the subscription level, preventing their delivery if they are no longer needed.
